analysis.title: US EQUITIES COLOR: CATCH DOWN
key_insights: Equities closed the week lower as broader semis and AI thematics 'caught down' to NVDA. Callahan's view: the 'rubber band' in semis got stretched too far.
Macro has tightened again: VIX at 20, 10-year yield back at 5.13% following a hot CPI, USD breaking out, oil back in the high-$90s.
Week-to-date action was rotational: NVDA shed about $500bn of market cap while AMD and AVGO combined added about $500bn or more.

GS flows showed heavy NVDA supply from the long-only community, with dollars rotating into hyperscalers and other large-cap tech. Both long-only and hedge fund cohorts finished the week as moderate net sellers.
Debate on the broader semis landscape continues as investors digest recent news flow (Nvidia and the election).
Week ahead: S&P implied move through Friday 11/20 is 1.93%. NVDA reports Tuesday, its first report under interim CEO Colette Kress, and BABA reports Thursday.
Prime book: hedge funds net sold US equities for a second straight week (5 of the last 6), driven by single-stock short sales partly offset by short covers and long buys in macro products.
US ETF shorts fell 8.6%, the largest percentage covering in 7 months. 8 of 11 sectors were net sold, led by Info Tech, Financials, Healthcare and Staples.
US Fundamental L/S gross leverage rose 1.6 pts to 209.1% (34th percentile one-year). Net leverage rose 2.1 pts to 45.4% (4th percentile one-year).
Net selling in US Financials this week was the largest in 8 months (99th percentile over 5 years).
earnings_insights: Earnings calendar next week: TSN and ARMK Monday, HD Tuesday, TJX, TGT and LOW Wednesday, WMT, ROST and GAP Thursday, BJ Friday.
NVDA reports Tuesday, its first report under interim CEO Colette Kress. BABA reports Thursday. GS flags both as key AI catalysts.
